tagline: A room with the harbour in it
sector: A fourteen-room design-led micro-hotel in a converted harbour warehouse, sold direct.
founded_place_size: Opened 2023 on the Nordhavn waterfront, Copenhagen; fourteen rooms run by one small owner-led team.
about: Nordhaven is a fourteen-room hotel inside a converted brick and timber warehouse on the working harbour. We sell the feeling of the building: cold light, plaster, oak and brass. Guests choose us because the place looks like nowhere else, and everything we make has to carry that.
audience: Design-literate urban travellers, 30 to 45, who choose a property on aesthetic and book direct once they trust the point of view.
price_positioning: Six hundred dollars a night, direct only, positioned above the travel-platform grid as a design destination rather than a room count.

typography: Nordhaven runs Zodiak Light for display and Söhne for text. Step 01, display and H1, is Zodiak Light at 96 px on 101 px, tracked minus 10 units: the one word room name in limewash on near black, with its floor and bed label locked directly beneath in Söhne Medium caps at 18 px on 22 px tracked 220 units, a fifth the size; the same name runs 72 px on 76 px in the room list. Step 02, the subheading, is Zodiak Light at 56 px on 62 px, tracked minus 5 units, the amenity heading. Step 03, body, is Söhne Regular at 24 px on 36 px, tracking 0, measure held to 65 characters, covering supporting lines, running text and amenities. Step 04, fine print, is Söhne Regular at 18 px on 26 px, tracked plus 20 units, and carries the rate. A rate is never set larger than its room name.
voice: Spare, understated, first person, no exclamation. Example line: 'Fourteen rooms on the water. We open direct booking this autumn.'
brand_assets_status: We work from a short brand note that fixes the near-black ground, the placements and the delivered sizes. There is no full guideline system yet, and the room list changes each season.
values: One committed tone across everything, with the true-colour main room photograph kept as the single deliberate exception so guests see the actual bed and linen.

palette_rules.distribution: Near-black ink #14161A is the ground of the booking hero and the amenity panel and the field behind every room name. Limewash plaster #E7E2D8 is the only other ground or panel, as on nordhaven_room_card_2025.pdf. Every room name is Limewash plaster on Near-black ink; other type on Near-black ink is Limewash plaster, and type on Limewash plaster is Near-black ink. Harbour slate, Oak and Brass are accents for hairline rules, dividers and icons only, together no more than 5% of the designed, non-photographic area, never a ground, a panel or any type.
palette_rules.opacity: Every palette colour is used solid, at 100% opacity. No tint, transparency, gradient, shadow or blend mode is applied to any palette colour, and no scrim, gradient or overlay of any colour, black and white included, is laid over a photograph: type sits on a solid Near-black ink or Limewash plaster ground or panel, beside the photograph or over it as a solid block, never directly on photographic pixels.
palette_rules.forbidden: No colour outside the five palette hexes for type, panels, rules, buttons or icons; no drop shadow or gradient on any of them, since every palette colour is used solid; nothing cheerful or saturated, as the brand note asks.
palette_rules.photography: Apart from the main room photograph on the booking hero, which stays true colour with no tint, tone or overlay, every photograph on every output, amenity cut-outs included, carries the same one committed tone, restrained and cold as the brand is, never cheerful or saturated. The two visits are brought onto one base before that tone is committed, and the tone may change colour and contrast but never what a subject or material is.
